title: clocks.json — the module's clock definitions (authored, never derived)
description: The sole numeric + relationship source for constraints/<TOP>.{sdc,sgdc} and for the TB clock generators. Exactly one entry is relationship=='primary'; derive-constraints checks this.

name.description: For a non-generated clock this is also the top-level port name create_clock binds to.

period_ns.description: Nominal period in ns. The TB uses it for input clock-port generators; a DUT-produced clock is observed from the implementation, not recreated from this number.

io_delay_ns.description: The arrival budget for every non-clock port in this domain, in ns: how much of the period is spent outside this module before an input is stable, and is left for whoever consumes an output. It reaches synthesis and timing-analysis as set_input_delay / set_output_delay, so it decides their verdicts. Optional, because a budget is a contract with whatever sits outside the chip and a module document often does not state one: write it when a requirements row gives it or the human rules one at the ledger and boundary gate, and leave it out otherwise — omitted, the SDC times the domain at 0, which is what an unallocated budget means, and says so in a comment. A ruling that the budget is unallocated leaves the field out: the SDC's 0 already carries it, and the ruling's words live in the stage's decisions. Never a fraction of the period.

relationship.description: async clocks drive set_clock_groups -asynchronous (SDC) and a distinct -domain (SGDC).

generated.description: true for a DUT-generated clock, internal or exposed at an output. derive-constraints defers create_generated_clock to the implemented source; it does not create an independent clock. Omitted means false.
